How Maps Harden Territorial Claims

📅 2026-08-19 ✍️ Henry Yep, Lowy Institute 🏷️ cartography, geopolitics, South China Sea, territorial claims, map regulation, sovereignty disputes, dashed-line map
🔗 Read the source article →

💡 Quick summary

The Lowy Institute analyzes how maps serve as tools of geopolitical power, examining how China's dashed-line map and state map regulation harden territorial claims by compressing complex legal questions into single authoritative images.

📌 Key takeaways

  • Maps can cast one side as lawful occupant and another as intruder in sovereignty disputes
  • China's dashed-line map, attached to 2009 diplomatic notes, enclosed most of the South China Sea without explaining the dashes' legal effect
  • China regulates public maps through official review, making unauthorized depictions of its territory illegal
  • The Ministry of Natural Resources runs an annual publicity week to promote national-territory awareness
  • Maps compress complex unsettled questions of land and water rights into a single image
  • When governments consistently present contested space as national territory, domestic compromise becomes harder
